title: fix(runtime)!: the dispatcher's read points refuse a repeated single-valued query name, as their RestServer twins do
body:
Part of #23214
Clause-②: yes (narrowing)

Slice 1 of #23214, under the seat ruling `6144365165` (option A: guard first, then flip) and claim `6144390225`. #23214 remains open: slice 2, the `createHonoApp` adapter flip, is the change that ends it, and it is dispatched only after this one lands.

## What this does

The runtime dispatcher's read points each read a query name as ONE value. None of them guarded against the name arriving twice, because the only door in front of most of them, the `@objectstack/hono` `createHonoApp` catch-all, has always flattened a repeat to its last value. Slice 2 will make that adapter keep repeats as arrays, as `plugin-hono-server`'s `readQuery` does. Round 1 measured what these points answer to the array shape (`os-dev-report` `6144314970`): wrong `200`s, arrays forwarded into protocol calls, and `500`s. Each point now refuses a repeated single-valued name with its `RestServer` twin's code and sentence, before any protocol or service call it feeds. A name sent once is answered as before, and one sent once as a one-element array now reads as that value.

## The points

Before = the answer to a repeat handed to `dispatch()` as an array (measured in round 1). After = this PR. Every "after" is `400` in the dispatcher's envelope, `{ success: false, error: { code, message } }`. The message is `repeatedQueryParamMessage(name, n)` (the multiplicity sentence), except on the `/data` filter slot.

| route | name(s) | twin's rule | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /meta/object/:name/state/:field` | `from` | `RestServer` refuses `['from']` | `200`, `from: 'done,todo'`, `next: []` (a dead end for a state that does not exist) | `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` |
| `GET /meta/_drafts` | `packageId`, `type` | `RestServer` refuses both | the array reached `listDrafts` | `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` |
| `GET /meta/:type` | `package`, `preview`, `object`, `include`, `id` | `RestServer` refuses all five | `object`: `200 []`; `package`: an unscoped list of every package; `preview`, `id`, `include`: read as absent | `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` |
| `GET /meta/book/:name/tree` | `package` | `RestServer` refuses it | read as absent: the tree spans every package | `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` |
| `GET /ui/view/:object` (no type segment) | `type` | no REST twin reads `?type` (REST mounts `/ui/view/:object/:type`) | the array reached `getUiView` | `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` |
| `GET /i18n/translations`, `GET /i18n/labels/:object` (no locale segment) | `locale` | no REST twin | `TypeError` in `resolveLocale`, so a `500` | `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` |
| `GET /security/suggested-bindings` | `status`, `packageId` | `RestServer` refuses both, in that order | `packageId`: joined to `'a,b'`, `200 []`; `status`: `400` with the unknown-status sentence | `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, multiplicity sentence |
| `GET /packages` | `status`, `type` | this domain's own `enabled` refusal | `===` against an array: `200` with no packages | `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` |
| `GET /data/:object` | the filter slot (`filter`, `where` and their aliases, `filters`, `$filter`) | `RestServer`'s list asks `assertFilterParamSuppliedOnce` | the array reached `findData`, where a filter AST is an array too | `400 INVALID_FILTER`, `RestServer`'s repeated-filter sentence |

Not touched: genuinely multi-valued names (`select` and `expand` stay arrays, pinned on the `/data` list), `?locale=` on the `/meta` doors (its one reader falls back to the default locale on both transports by design), and the four by-name `/meta` doors, which already ask `metaItemQueryRefusal`.

## One source for the `/meta` arity lists

`RestServer` spelled four `/meta` arity lists inline: the list door, the book tree, `_drafts` and the state machine read. They move to `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts` beside `metaItemQueryRefusal`, as `META_QUERY_ARITY_DOORS`, with the decision `metaQueryArityRefusal(door, query)`. `RestServer` hands each list to `refuseRepeatedQueryParams`, re-pointed in spelling only, and the dispatcher asks the decision over the same list. `metaItemQueryRefusal`'s rule 2 and the new decision share one private implementation of the rule.

**Byte-identity proof: a BASE/HEAD differential**, because the unchanged REST pins cover only `object` and `package` on the list door. It ran 50 cases through `RestServer`'s four route handlers: every declared name twice and three times, as a one-element array, as an empty array and as one value; two repeated names; an undeclared repeat; and no query. It recorded each status, body, headers and protocol call. The BASE leg ran with the three rest files restored from `06dbc4e59d` into the tree only. The HEAD leg ran at `45db8870ca`, after a restore proven by an empty `git diff HEAD` and matching blob hashes. The two dumps are byte-identical (`cmp` silent; sha256 prefix `c63cb9403588e830` on both; 18 refusals among the 50 cases). The scratch harness was never committed. `meta-query-arity-doors.test.ts` also pins that `RestServer` refuses exactly the names the shared list declares, door by door, so the list is the one both read.

**Scope note, stated rather than chosen silently.** The dispatch names the list door (`:6013`) and the book tree (`:6288`) as the lists that move, and groups I1, I2, S1, S2, U1 and `/packages` as points with no shared list. `_drafts` (`:5861`) and the state read (`:8225`) are in neither group, but they are `/meta` doors whose twins spell an arity list. So they moved too, under the ruling's general rule ("where `RestServer` spells an arity list, that list moves"), which the claim's `rest-server.ts` surface ("the arity lists' spelling") allows. `/security/suggested-bindings`' twin also spells a list (`['status', 'packageId']`), but `meta-item-read-gate.ts` is no home for a security route, and the dispatch places it in the no-shared-list group. So the dispatcher spells those two names at its own read point beside the shared sentence. That is a second spelling of a two-name list, recorded below.

## The `/data` filter slot

`assertFilterParamSuppliedOnce` joins `@objectstack/rest`'s entry (it was already exported from `query-multiplicity.ts`; that file is untouched). The dispatcher's `/data` list asks it on the copy `findData` receives, and answers its throw in the dispatcher's envelope with the code (`INVALID_FILTER`) and sentence it carries. `FILTER_SLOT_QUERY_PARAMS` is not exported: the dispatcher does not need the list itself. The pin computes REST's expected answer by calling the same imported rule, never by re-spelling it.

## Census: who sends a repeat to these routes today

- **`@objectstack/client` (SDK):** every swept name is written with `URLSearchParams.set` or a single template (`?from=`, `?package=`), and `ui.getView` and the i18n reads put the type and locale in the path. The only `append` calls are `data.find`'s plain filter map, which writes each key of one object once. No repeat.
- **objectui at the console pin `.objectui-sha` `1fb1ced362`** (a read-only depth-1 fetch; nothing executed): direct requests to these paths are single-occurrence templates (`/api/v1/meta/_drafts?packageId=…`, `GET /meta/object?package=…&preview=draft`). Its three non-example `URLSearchParams.append` sites build the console's own browser URL state (`filter[…]`, `uf_*`), not API requests.
- **dogfood and http-conformance suites, and every string literal under `packages/` and `examples/`** (8,595 files scanned): the only literal repeats target REST routes this PR does not change, in REST's own multiplicity test. There are no `append` calls in `packages/qa` and no array-valued queries handed to `dispatch()` on these routes.

So, as mechanism assumption 1 expected, the narrowing is visible on a shipped host only at `GET /packages` through `plugin-hono-server`, whose adapter already keeps repeats as arrays. Everywhere else it is visible only to a direct `HttpDispatcher.dispatch()` caller that passes an array, until slice 2. The changeset says so.

## Read only: the dispatcher's `DELETE /data/:object/:id`

**Measurable at a public door: yes.** Driven through the real `createHonoApp` over the real dispatcher, with a recording `deleteData`: `DELETE /api/v1/data/task/r1?expectedVersion=7` and the same request with `If-Match: "7"` both answer `200`, and `deleteData` receives `{ object: 'task', id: 'r1' }` with no version. That is identical to a request that sends none. `RestServer`'s twin forwards `expectedVersion` (query or `If-Match`) to `deleteData`. So on a `createHonoApp` host a caller's optimistic-concurrency guard is silently dropped. Not changed here, per the dispatch.

## Responsibility

`git blame` at `06dbc4e59d` for each swept read line, not shallow. All of them are later than the flattening's origin, `6ac9f8c96f` (2026-02-13). Most come from the ADR-0076 D11 domain extractions of 2026-07-27 (`8891f93948` for `/meta` and `/data`, `21ca1d530c` for `/ui`, `8f124a7b77` for `/i18n` and `/security`, `d729a31160` for `/packages`), which moved older `http-dispatcher.ts` code. The `/data` list line is `fd8521f923` (2026-08-04); the `/meta` list's `preview` is `5c7aa46748` and the view switcher's `object` `95f729a1ad` (both 2026-09-28); `?package=` on the list and book tree is `fbcbcf124f` (2026-10-08); and `/security` `status` is `bca935b9ac` (2026-07-30). #6877's sweep commit `f3f855ac15` (2026-08-10) touched no runtime domain or dispatcher file. The two later commits citing #6877 that edited `domains/meta.ts` (`7986d973fa`, `d2b2381a36`) added no arity rule there. So the claim's reading holds: these points were written or moved behind an adapter that flattened repeats, and #6877 covered `packages/rest` only.

- `@objectstack/runtime`: `vitest run --project local`: 368 files passed, 5254 tests passed, 19 skipped, `VERDICT command-exit 0`. Before the merge, at `11725bfec8`: 367 files, 5238 passed.
- `@objectstack/rest`: `vitest run --project local`: 279 files passed, 5831 tests passed, 326 skipped, `VERDICT command-exit 0`. Before the merge: 278 files, 5825 passed.
- `meta-list-projection-parity` (runtime `repo` project): 739 passed.
- Typecheck, both packages (`tsc --noEmit` plus `check:test-typecheck`): exit 0. Runtime test-layer debt is unchanged (27 files, 190 errors, 68 signatures); rest's is 0.
- The derived gate list (`dispatch-gates --commands`, no paths, 65 commands) ran each with its exit captured before any pipe: 64 exit 0. One is NOT MEASURED: `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exits 3, `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (it reads every package's `dist/`; a full build here is 31 turbo cache misses including `@objectstack/console`, so CI runs it). As a scoped supplement, the CJS builds of `@objectstack/rest` and `@objectstack/runtime` load under `require`, and rest's carries the three new exports. `--ran` reconciliation: "65 derived, 64 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN".
- Named by the dispatch: `pnpm check:adr-0087-registration` exit 0 (`[BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing] not-required (no-migration-prescription)`); `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main` exit 0, plus its `--event` form on this PR's title and body; `pnpm check:route-envelope` exit 0; `pnpm check:nul-bytes` exit 0.
- Lint, as a proven narrowing over the 11 touched `.ts` files. Population: the config's own `files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}']` block, with none of the 11 ignored. Count: `--format json` reports 11 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 fatal. Invariance: `eslint.config.mjs` never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no typed rules), so this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict.

## Ablations (restore traps; restores proven by `git diff HEAD` and blob hash)

Each leg ran through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (WRAP; the anchor hit once, its count went from 1 to 0, and the blob moved). No build or `dist` leg applies: the pins reach the code under test through relative imports, and runtime's vitest aliases `@objectstack/rest` to its source (`packages/runtime/vitest.config.ts:149`).

| leg | mutation | red | green |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/meta` | remove the `state` door's refusal | 1 (`from` refusal) | 32, including the `from` preservation |
| `/ui` | short-circuit the array branch | 1 (`type` refusal) | 32 |
| `/i18n` | raise the repeat threshold to 99 | 2 (both arms' refusals) | 31, including the preservation |
| `/security` | raise the repeat threshold to 99 | 2 (`status`, `packageId`) | 31 |
| `/packages` | raise the repeat threshold to 99 | 2 (`status`, `type`) | 31 |
| `/data` | delete the `assertFilterParamSuppliedOnce(listQuery)` call | 5 (four filter spellings, plus the one-element unwrap, which is the rule's own) | 28, including the one-filter preservation |

No preservation pin went red in any leg.

## Acceptance notes

- `/security/suggested-bindings` carries a second spelling of `['status', 'packageId']`, beside `RestServer`'s twin, as the dispatch directed. A shared home for non-`/meta` arity lists would end it; it was not created here.
- The book tree and `_drafts` refuse at the point `RestServer` refuses: after the protocol is looked up, and for `_drafts` after the capability gate and the `listDrafts` probe. The `/data` filter refusal answers before `callData`'s exposure gate, where `RestServer` answers after its own. For a repeated filter on an object whose API is not exposed, this transport therefore answers `400` before `403`.
- New `@objectstack/rest` exports: `META_QUERY_ARITY_DOORS`, `metaQueryArityRefusal` and `assertFilterParamSuppliedOnce`. The door type is not exported, matching `metaItemQueryRefusal`'s.
